completion:
Identify faults in the test.
3. Record the test faults.
4. Determine the course of action.
5. Mark test records and then close records.

by Michael Coughlin
For the last six years, I have been conducting residual current device (RCD) and electrical appliance safety checks. During this time I have studied how to evaluate a test, record test results, and structure the results to have the required documents meet all legal requirements. Through trial and error, I have developed a testing process to record test results in a checklist using precisely worded statements. This is a representation of my documented experiences with and my recommendations for preparing work instructions and completing paperwork for failed appliance checks.

## Starting with the test records

To conduct a test successfully, it is required I understand both the theory and field procedures for the equipment that I am testing and record the test results accurately. Most company procedures are incomplete or inadequate and cost a business
